modules.name: cli
modules.responsibility: Parse argv into commands (add/remove/list/complete), render output, map exit codes. No business logic or persistence.

modules.name: core
modules.responsibility: Task domain logic: create, complete, delete, list with filtering/ordering. Enforces invariants (unique id, non-empty title).

modules.name: storage
modules.responsibility: Persist and retrieve tasks behind a repository Protocol. Default JSON-file implementation; swappable for SQLite.

fields.name: completed_at
fields.description: UTC completion timestamp, null if open

ux_flows.name: Add task
steps: TaskService creates Task with new id
ux_flows.success_criteria: New task persisted and id echoed; exit code 0
error_states: Empty title -> exit 2 with usage message
Storage write failure -> exit 1 with error, no partial write

ux_flows.name: List tasks
ux_flows.success_criteria: Open tasks shown ordered by created_at; exit code 0
error_states: Corrupt store -> exit 1 with recovery hint

ux_flows.name: Complete task
ux_flows.success_criteria: Task flagged done idempotently; exit code 0
error_states: Unknown id -> exit 2 with not-found message

customer_journey: A developer installs todo-cli and immediately runs `todo add` to capture a task without configuration. They check `todo list` to see open work, mark items `todo done`, and trust that state survives across invocations via a local JSON file. The tool stays out of the way: fast, scriptable, predictable exit codes, and no network. When they outgrow JSON they swap the repository for SQLite with no change to commands.

experience_metric.name: time-to-first-task
experience_metric.target: User adds and lists their first task in <= 2 commands with zero configuration
experience_metric.measurement: Count commands from fresh install to successful `todo list` showing the added task

architecture_decisions.title: Repository Protocol abstracts persistence
architecture_decisions.context: Tasks must persist locally, but the storage backend may evolve (JSON file now, SQLite later).
architecture_decisions.decision: Define a TaskRepository Protocol; inject a concrete JSON-file implementation into TaskService.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Dependency inversion keeps core logic free of I/O concerns and makes the service unit-testable with an in-memory fake.
consequences: Requires DI wiring at the composition root

architecture_decisions.title: Inject Clock and IdGenerator
architecture_decisions.context: Tasks carry timestamps and ids; tests need determinism.
architecture_decisions.decision: Provide Clock and IdGenerator Protocols injected into the service rather than calling datetime.now()/ULID inline.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Deterministic, reproducible tests and no hidden global state.
consequences: Two extra injection points to wire

threat_model.description: Malicious or corrupt JSON store causes deserialization errors or injected fields.
threat_model.mitigation: Validate loaded data through Pydantic models; reject unknown fields; atomic write via temp-file-and-rename.

threat_model.description: Task titles may contain sensitive user content readable by other local users.
threat_model.mitigation: Store under user-owned path with 0600 permissions; document that contents are plaintext local data.

threat_model.description: Concurrent invocations race on the store file and clobber writes.
threat_model.mitigation: Acquire an advisory file lock around read-modify-write; atomic rename on save.

privacy_inventory.retention: Until user deletes the task or clears the store
privacy_inventory.encryption: At-rest relies on OS filesystem permissions (0600); no app-level encryption
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: `todo remove <id>` deletes the entry; deleting the store file erases all

i18n_plan.rtl_strategy: Renderer detects RTL locales (he) and aligns columns right-to-left; titles preserved as UTF-8 without reshaping

open_questions: Should completed tasks be retained indefinitely or auto-pruned after N days?
Is file-lock-based concurrency sufficient, or is SQLite needed in v1 to close threat D?

sections.title: Module Boundaries
sections.content: Three layers: cli (parsing/rendering), core (TaskService domain logic), storage (TaskRepository Protocol). Dependencies flow cli -> core -> storage; storage depends on nothing. DI at composition root injects repository, clock, and id generator.

sections.title: Data Model
sections.content: Single Task entity: id (ULID), title (non-empty), done (bool), created_at, completed_at. No relationships. Title classified user-content.

sections.title: UX Flows
sections.content: add, list (open by default, --all for completed), done. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 storage error, 2 usage/not-found. All messages localizable.

sections.title: Architecture Decisions
sections.content: ADR-001 Repository Protocol for swappable persistence. ADR-002 Inject Clock and IdGenerator for deterministic tests.

sections.title: Security & Privacy
sections.content: STRIDE: tampering/info-disclosure mitigated via validated atomic writes and 0600 perms; concurrent-write DoS open pending file lock. Titles are user-content with deletion-based erasure path.
